review_run.feedback: With 376 items and a small budget I judged mostly from commit subjects, not by opening code or task files, so many 'partly' and 'done' ratings rest on a subject line alone. Three changes would help. Pre-link each item to candidate commits or task paths, so evidence lookup is one step instead of a search. Mark questions and statements the owner already had answered in chat, so they are not judged again. Merge duplicate items such as p214.10 and p214.14, and the many 'note' statements from one dictation. CLAUDE.md update items would also be easier to check if the evidence listed whether that file changed in the window.

review_run.feedback: I judged almost everything from the commit subject leads and task folder names without opening the code, so many 'done' marks rest on subject-line matches. Items are a mix of real asks, one-off questions, and remarks, and the file hint is often CLAUDE.md or a skill with no way to check whether the line landed. The cands lists were noisy: many were only a shared word, such as 'handover' or 'skills'. It would help to give each cand its changed file paths, to mark the owner's reply to a question when it exists, and to give every item the id of the follow-up item that settled it, so 'option' and 'rejected' states can be set from evidence.
